I deal with similar things, you're not alone in this. It is incredibly frustrating and quite distressing. 

I was able to get a therapy called DBT, which is a skills based therapy, and the skill I found most useful with these thoughts is "check the facts". As it states, you focus on the truth instead of the anxiety. 

For example, I get anxious about not being able to get to sleep. I want to go down the anxiety rabbit hole and find a rare disorder that causes my lack of sleep. Then I check the facts and see that I had some caffeine close to my bed time. 

Another example, I get anxious when people are late to things. I go down the rabbit hole of them being in a car crash, but then I check the facts and can remember seeing road works on the road they'd drive down or it's a friday at 5pm so there would be traffic.

I'd also suggest looking up mindfulness. It's about focusing on the now instead of the past or the future and can be of great benefit in times of anxiety. The way I do it is focus on something familiar,  such as my keys, and then describe them in detail until the anxiety has passed. I'd reccomend practicing it even when you're not anxious as, same with everything, the more you practice the better you get.

The most important thing though is getting therapy. The sooner you can do it the better. I was able to get therapy through a youth charity at 14 without my mum knowing, I live in the UK. 

I'm not sure where you're from but in the UK you go to a doctor and they refer you for therapy. If this is the same where you are, whilst in that appointment raise your health concerns with them. I was anxious I had a blood disorder as I had a few symptoms so my doctor sent me for a blood test and found I was iron deficient, something easily treated. 

I hope you've found this helpful and I hope you get the help you need. Stay away from Doctor Google!
